title: AI Engineering 201: The Rest of the Owl
talk_summary: A survey talk on patterns for building LLM products: RAG/information retrieval, structured outputs via JSON schema and grammar-based sampling, agents with cognitive architectures, and monitoring/observability/evaluation. It is mostly conceptual and pre-agent-era, with few measured results, but several mechanisms (schema-enforced outputs, fake function calls for classification, LLM-as-annotator, iterated decomposition for evals) are directly copyable.

takeaways.technique: Schema-enforced structured outputs (JSON schema / function-call format)
takeaways.what_they_do: Force model output into a JSON schema (via function-calling format, retry-on-invalid, or grammar-based sampling that zeroes out tokens violating the grammar) so downstream systems can parse it reliably.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it would violate some grammar if it would violate some template or format just set the probability of generating that to zero

takeaways.technique: Fake function call for classification decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking the model to judge, define a fictional function whose arguments encode the decision (e.g. is_spam: bool) and read the arguments; the model commits to a structured verdict.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can tell it about a fake function that's like please pass a string like describing whether the the input was spam or not spam

takeaways.technique: Iterated decomposition of failing tasks into simpler subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the task end-to-end, inspect failures, split the task so the failure surfaces in a simpler subtask, then optimize/evaluate that subtask in isolation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you Noti notice a failure you look at the failures and you see how you could have broken the task out into multiple pieces

takeaways.what_they_do: Use LLMs to label/annotate data for evals, claiming GPT-3.5 ≈ median crowd worker and GPT-4 ≈ 90th percentile, cheaper than human annotation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: gbd 3.5 turbo is like a median crowd worker gbd4 is like a 90th percentile crowd worker
takeaways.numbers: GPT-3.5 ≈ median crowd worker; GPT-4 ≈ 90th percentile crowd worker

takeaways.what_they_do: Combine keyword and vector search, and extract metadata with an LLM to pre-filter before vector search rather than post-filtering results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: extracting metadata with a language model so that you can then use that to do like direct filtering

takeaways.technique: Cognitive-architecture framing for agent memory/decision procedures
takeaways.what_they_do: Borrow procedural/semantic/episodic memory and explicit decision procedures from classical cognitive architectures, using the LLM for world knowledge and the structure for memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how to implement that in software and the problem like those systems could do cool stuff but the problem is always that they lacked this like General World Knowledge
